chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Unive
spiritual_reading:
When he had come into a state where living truth was flowing through the midst of his understanding, he turned his perception away from a merely natural confidence. He perceived that if the whole sufficient series of merely outward expressions that arise from the natural self were set forth in the outermost plane of life, and even if they were arranged into an apparent harmony there, they would still fail when compared with what is truly elevated in the Lord. They could not rise into the same degree of interior life, nor extend into the same fullness of intelligence, nor open into the same breadth of wisdom, nor descend into the same ultimate completeness, because they do not share the Lord’s Divine quality from first to last.

Nor is this the only difference: even if every one of those outward expressions, from the least to the greatest, were gathered into one general body of knowledges and made to appear as a single comprehensive doctrine, they would still be absorbed and lost within that generality, and their life would be extinguished within the natural plane. Yet within that outward plane there still exist many elevated states that can be made great in form. These, in their better condition, do not set themselves against the holy stillness of Divine order; they do not speak denial against the wisdom that enlightens, nor against the Divine power that holds all things in connection, nor against the Divine reality that shines through all things and gives them their total form, nor against the goods that proceed from justice. In that better condition they do not fabricate an origin of evil from the Divine.

But the self-made religious principle of ill-fated humanity, which exalts what is unlike the Divine as though it were equal and claims greatness for itself, was found to be evil by the Lord of all. It spoke denial against the Divine power that holds all things together and against the holy wisdom that gives light; it violated the glory of Divine intelligence, and from that violation it produced the root of sin. From it arose the assertion that every shameful evil and every defilement, all the dominant evils and the hellish persuasions and the destroyers and the adversarial falsities, are from the Divine itself, as though the Lord had established them. Yet they do not come from him; this is a falsifying testimony against the Divine.

The Lord did not enter into the outermost plane and deliver it for the sake of the human race alone, but in order to reveal in that plane what had power beyond it and to set in order what was disordered in the whole expanse of created degrees. When he had completed this work in the outermost level of the universal order, he advanced further, conjoining the first formed good and the first formed truth to himself, and opened to them what had been hidden. In the same way he sent those who would teach, to those who are capable of receiving good, age after age, and he disclosed to them a sufficient set of great essentials.

Second: he opened to them the ordered successions of the heavenly states of life, how they arise and take form; and he also taught them about the mode of falsity and obscurity, how it too is permitted to exist.

Third: he announced to them the greatness of Divine wisdom, how it has acted against the power of falsity and has overcome it.

Fourth: he taught that he entered into the state of spiritual death that reigns in the merely natural self, until he could find what could receive benefit, and raise them out of the lowest captivity in which they had been held and from which they could not free themselves.

All who are faithful, and who believe this truth with an inward acknowledgment, will have spiritual life from three great and mighty essentials, though what these three are is not fully expressed in this portion of the text.

fills.notes: The spiritual sense says “outward expressions … were set forth in the outermost plane.” The substrate register prefers impersonal manifestation-language (appear, be shown) rather than moralizing terms.
Corresponds to assembling the “five words” into the outer plane as a complete set; fits the following “set them in order … with one another.”
The spiritual sense explicitly: “out from … which is deep.” In the Iranian-cosmological substrate, the deep source opposed to the heights is regularly expressed as an abyssal depth.
The next clause: “They will make it like [ … ] and they set them in order …” demands a collective form (one corpus) made from the five, before ordering.

fills.fill: and they set them in order
fills.notes: The visible remnants include “with o”; the sense requires arrangement into an apparent harmony in the external plane.
Spiritual sense: they “fail when compared” and “could not rise.” The natural image is attempted ascent “up to the heights.”
The comparison-series height, breadth, width, depth demands a repeated proportional formula rather than a unique phrase.
The phrase “from their smallest to their greatest” is fixed by the spiritual sense (“from the least to the greatest”).
The sentence contrasts multiplicity with being made “a single sea … single …”: thus a gathering into one generality.
Supplies the needed article before “single sea,” matching the repeated “single …”.
Spiritual sense: “one general body of knowledges … a single comprehensive doctrine.” The natural correspondent is a sea as a total mass; “whole depth” preserves the impersonal cosmological register.
The clause “they are swallowed and …” requires the consequent extinction of distinct things within the sea; “drowned” matches the sea-correspondence (life extinguished in mere generality).
Spiritual sense: “absorbed and lost … and their life would be extinguished.” Natural counterpart: loss of distinct form in the sea.
Governs the following “earth … many mountains … sea in it”: i.e., within this same outer plane.
Turns from drowning-in-the-sea to the contrasting fact: “Yet within that outward plane there still exist many elevated states.”
Links “many mountains … sea in it” to the concession “even if” in the spiritual sense (better condition within the same plane).
Mountains correspond to elevated states; “stand forth” keeps the impersonal descriptive tone and prepares “very great in their fashion.”
The surviving letters constrain “fashion”; the spiritual sense requires a contrast (“These … can be made great in form. These … do not set themselves against …”).
Directly matches the spiritual translation’s qualifier, distinguishing these mountains from the blaspheming idol in ¶4.
Prepares “the silence” as the stillness of Divine order; corresponds to not setting themselves against holy order.
The spiritual sense: “they do not fabricate an origin of evil from the Divine.” Substrate register prefers “attribute” (impersonal causal assignment) over moral exhortation.
Spiritual sense: “self-made religious principle … exalts what is unlike the Divine.” The natural text needs an action of self-exaltation introducing the comparison “unlike … equal … great works.”

fills.fill: to the power and the essence
fills.notes: This paragraph immediately repeats “power … light … wisdom.” The idol claims equality with what in the substrate are the Divine sustaining power and manifest essence; hence this pairing fits the correspondential structure.
Closes the claim “he is the one who established them …”: the substrate polemic is about attributing the origin of evil to the Divine as first cause.
Balances “not … because of mankind alone, but …” and transitions to purpose: revealing and ordering, as in the spiritual translation.
Spiritual sense: “reveal … what had power beyond it.” This matches the extant “was strong outside …”.
Corresponds to “the whole expanse of created degrees” and fits “outside in …” without devotional coloring.
The broken “... he wen” plus the spiritual sense “he advanced further” indicates forward movement after completing the outer work.

Spiritual sense: “state of spiritual death that reigns in the merely natural self.” The natural correspondent given by the text is “flesh”; this fill supplies the reigning quality (province) without later institutional language.

assessment: Most lacunae are small letter-restorations with strong constraint. The larger gaps in ¶2–4 are recoverable to a moderate degree by the chapter’s fixed correspondence-series: (1) assembling outward expressions, (2) arranging them externally, (3) failed comparison with the mountain’s discrete measures, (4) drowning of particulars in a single sea (mere generality), (5) the contrasting non-blaspheming mountains, and (6) the idol’s self-exaltation and false attribution of evil’s origin to the Divine. Two larger fills (¶3 #12 and ¶4 #4) remain tentative because the surviving English synopsis does not preserve enough of the underlying Coptic syntagms to lock a single phrasing beyond the demanded spiritual function.
